title: Variational Consequence-Driven Offline Reinforcement Learning
claim: Matching distributions directly in action space ignores downstream consequences, and the ideal consequence-space constraint is intractable. A latent surrogate is tractable and closed-form.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, curved arrows linking spaces, ✗/✓ icons below
description: Three spaces are laid out left to right and linked by curved dark-navy arrows. On the left, titled Action Space, a green blob for the learned policy π(a|s) overlaps a blue blob for the behavior policy π_β(a|s). A curved arrow between them is labeled KL/MMD. A red prohibition icon sits below with the text 'Neglects dynamic consistency'. In the middle, titled Gaussian Latent Space, a small green circle sits inside a larger blue circle, labeled 'closed-form KL'. A green check mark and the text 'Tractable surrogate' sit below it. On the right, titled State-Consequence Space, two irregular jagged blobs, green and blue, overlap and carry a KL arrow. A red prohibition icon with 'Intractable (unknown dynamics)' sits below. Arrows are labeled with the encoder p_ϑ(z|s,π) and the dynamics P(s'|s,π), both marked 'policy induced'. Green marks the learned policy and blue marks the behavior policy.
caption: Conceptual illustration of divergence-based behavior regularization. Purely action distribution matching (left) neglects dynamic consistency, whereas ideal consequence-aware constraints (right) are computationally intractable without access to the true dynamics. Our StBR (middle) employs a Gaussian latent space as a tractable, closed-form surrogate of consequence-aware constraints.
abstract: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) typically mitigates distribution shift by imposing divergence constraints on the action distributions of the learned and behavior policies. However, this paradigm cannot ensure the underlying dynamic consistency structure: even minor action deviations can lead to drastically different transitions, inadvertently driving the agent away from the offline dataset. To address this, we explore policy constraints through their induced state-consequence distributions rather than relying on pure action-distribution matching. Nevertheless, directly enforcing such consequence-aware constraints is computationally intractable without access to the true underlying dynamics model. To bypass this issue, we propose Structural Behavior Regularization (StBR), which replaces the intractable objective with a closed-form latent divergence. Structuring this latent space to reflect transition dynamics renders the latent divergence a theoretically bounded surrogate for the true consequence-distribution divergence. By regularizing the learned policy with this latent divergence, StBR adaptively tightens the behavior constraint in dynamics-sensitive regions, effectively preventing deviations outside the offline dataset. Empirically, we demonstrate that StBR achieves superior performance across diverse offline RL benchmarks.
